title: Nebius Group (NBIS) Has A Fresh Update, But What Is Drawing Attention Now?
detail:
Nebius Group (NBIS) Has A Fresh Update, But What Is Drawing Attention Now?
Simply Wall St
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 11:17 AM MST 4 min read
NBIS
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nebius Group (NBIS) has secured a new US$3.5 billion senior secured facility from Citi, providing the AI infrastructure provider with additional capital to fund data centers and GPU purchases.

Recent trading has been choppy for Nebius Group, with the share price falling 26.3% over the past 30 days and 22.4% over 90 days, even though the year-to-date share price return sits at 90.7% and the 1-year total shareholder return is 74.0%.

Short sellers have leaned into the pullback, with rising short interest and sector-wide concerns about debt-funded AI buildouts weighing on sentiment. This comes just as Nebius Group rolls out public GPU spot pricing, expands its European AI capacity and locks in the new US$3.5b Citi facility as near-term funding.

Scan how short-seller pressure and debt-funded buildouts are priced across AI infrastructure peers, and see which ones screen as potential outliers with 55 AI infrastructure stocks

Nebius Group is clearly building a large AI infrastructure platform, yet the share price has swung sharply while fresh Citi funding and new pricing tools land. Does that setup leave NBIS mispriced or roughly fair today?

Most Popular Narrative: 34% Undervalued

The most followed narrative on Nebius Group pegs fair value at about $260 per share, compared with the recent $171.57 close. As a result, the story now leans heavily on whether aggressive AI infrastructure spending actually converts into durable cash generation.

The $260 fair value represents our working estimate of what NBIS could be worth if the company delivers strong AI-cloud growth and improves profitability. It should be treated as an upside target rather than evidence that the shares are clearly cheap, because NBIS trades at approximately 42.3 times sales, compared with a peer average of approximately 9.8 times.

See why 21 investors see Nebius Group as 34% undervalued.

Result: Fair Value of $259.97 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the Nebius Group story can break if AI Cloud growth slows sharply, or if heavy debt and convertible funding keep free cash flow deeply negative.

Find out about the key risks to this Nebius Group narrative.

Another View: What Nebius Group's Sales Multiple Signals

The fair value narrative leans on long term growth and cash generation, yet the current pricing tells a sharper story. Nebius Group trades on a P/S of 34.7x, compared with about 4x for the wider US software industry and roughly 10.3x for peers, while the fair ratio is 35.8x.

The gap between 34.7x and a 35.8x fair ratio is slim. This points to a stock already priced close to what the regression model suggests the market could move toward. With such a small cushion and much richer levels than industry and peer averages, the remaining scope for mispricing appears limited.

title: Nebius signs $3.5 billion senior secured bridge loan with Citi
detail:
Nebius signs $3.5 billion senior secured bridge loan with Citi
William Foxley
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:56 AM MST 2 min read
NBIS
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Data center operator Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) disclosed Thursday a $3.5 billion senior secured bridge loan from Citi to fund GPU procurement and data center construction. The loan carries an initial rate of term SOFR plus 275 bps and matures October 16, 2027, a 364-day tenor.

The margin rises by 25 bps for each 90-day period after signing, capped at 350 bps. Nebius can prepay without premium or penalty. The only financial covenant is a minimum liquidity requirement.

The borrowers are parent Nebius Group N.V. and two subsidiaries, Nebius Inc. and Nebius B.V. Collateral covers substantially all assets of each borrower, including the parent's shares in both subsidiaries, excepting excluded assets and liens that are allowed. Citibank, N.A. is mandated lead arranger and lender, with affiliates acting as agent and security agent.

Stay ahead of AI infrastructure deals. Get Blockspace in your inbox.

Nebius debt

This loan is structured differently from Nebius' first secured debt. The $775 million loan announced in July was secured at the asset level by deployed GPUs and contracted cash flows from one investment-grade customer. It priced at SOFR plus 250 bps and runs to October 31, 2030, with MUFG leading and Citi as a senior lead arranger.

In August, Nebius closed $5.75 billion of convertible senior notes. The deal comprised $3.45 billion of 0.50% notes due 2030 and $2.30 billion of 4.50% notes due 2034, both senior unsecured obligations of the parent.

Chief Operating Officer Ophir Nave described the Citi loan as near-term construction capital, with longer-dated financing to follow:

"Sequencing our financing is how we optimize our long-term cost of capital. This facility provides additional financing to support our near-term capacity build-out. We still have a range of capital sources available to us to finance the next phase of growth, including asset-backed financing based on investment-grade customer commitments of more than $40 billion of long-term contracts," Nave said.

Nebius named Microsoft and Meta among the customers behind that $40 billion in its July announcement. The company has described the July structure as a repeatable asset-level framework.

Nebius kept 2026 capex guidance at $20 billion to $25 billion, along with a year-end connected-power target of 800 MW to 1 GW. In the second quarter, it spent $5.66 billion on property, equipment and intangibles against $2.25 billion of operating cash flow, and it ended June with $8.04 billion in cash.

Customer prepayments are the other funding source. About 70% of second-quarter deals included prepayments covering 50% to 60% of associated capex, Nebius said in its August shareholder letter. The company expects more than $9 billion in prepayments this year.

title: These 4 Big Banks Pay Similar Dividends. Their Balance Sheets Tell Another Story
detail:
These 4 Big Banks Pay Similar Dividends. Their Balance Sheets Tell Another Story
Chris Lange
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 8:45 AM MST 8 min read
JPM
BAC
WFC
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

JPMorgan's 25.8% payout ratio and 13.9% CET1 ratio are the highest among the four, ranking it the safest big bank dividend, with ~$30 billion in estimated excess capital.

Bank of America leads the group with the highest yield at 2.3% but carries the smallest capital buffer, just 90 basis points above its regulatory minimum.

Wells Fargo ranks last because it was the only bank to cut its dividend during the pandemic, slashing the quarterly payout from $0.51 to $0.10 in 2020.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

All four of America's largest banks have raised their quarterly payouts within the past six months: JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM), Citigroup (NYSE:C), Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) and Bank of America (NYSE:BAC). Even so, the group's best yield is only 2.3%. Because the yields are so close, what separates these four for an income portfolio is strength. That means how much of each bank's earnings the dividend uses, how much capital sits above the regulatory floor, and what each board did the last time a crisis hit. Every one of these banks has cut its dividend at least once in the modern era, so a bank's track record matters as much as its current payout (we laid out the seven warning signs that a big yield is about to be cut in a free report here).

Pixels Hunter / Shutterstock.com
JPMorgan Chase: The Fortress Payer With the Thickest Capital Cushion

JPMorgan yields 1.83% at a share price near $333. Among the four, the yield is the lowest, but the safety numbers are the strongest. The board just raised the quarterly dividend to $1.65 from $1.50, for an annualized forward payout of $6.60 per share.

Safety read: Trailing dividends of $6.15 against diluted EPS of $23.84 give a payout ratio of about 25.8%. JPMorgan ended the third quarter with a standardized CET1 ratio of 13.9%, the highest in this group. CEO Jamie Dimon estimated "probably $30 billion or something of excess capital", and the bank holds $1.5 trillion of cash and marketable securities. The track record is mixed but solid. JPMorgan cut its quarterly payout from $0.38 to $0.05 in 2009. In 2020, though, it held the dividend at $0.90 per quarter and has raised the payout repeatedly since then.

title: Nebius Says It Is ‘Sequencing’ Its Financing After Getting $3.5B From Citi, With Bigger Asset-Backed Loans Still to Come
detail:
Nebius Says It Is ‘Sequencing’ Its Financing After Getting $3.5B From Citi, With Bigger Asset-Backed Loans Still to Come
Prabhjote Gill
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 5:25 AM MST 4 min read
NBIS
C
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Chief Operating Officer Ophir Nave said the Citi funding shows Nebius can choose "when and how we raise capital."

According to him, the loan supports the company's near-term buildout, with larger financing still ahead.

He said the company has $40 billion in long-term customer contracts that could serve as collateral.

Nebius (NBIS) shares dipped in morning trade on Thursday amid the broader market sell-off after the company announced it had secured a $3.5 billion senior secured facility from Citi.

Chief Operating Officer Ophir Nave said it shows the Nvidia (NVDA)-backed company can choose "when and how we raise capital." The loan supports the near-term buildout, he said, and larger financing is still ahead.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

"Sequencing our financing is how we optimize our long-term cost of capital," Nave stated. "We still have a range of capital sources available to us to finance the next phase of growth." He added that the company currently has $40 billion in long-term customer contracts that could be used for collateral.

NBIS stock fell as much as 2.5% in pre-market trade and was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing, with retail traders debating whether the new loan aids the company's AI build out or increases debt risk.

Nebius Short-Term Funding

The facility matures in 364 days and initially carries an interest rate of Term SOFR plus 2.75%, rising to a maximum of 3.50%, subject to other adjustments. Nebius said proceeds will go toward data center development, GPU purchases and general corporate purposes.

However, the loan comes amid mounting pressure on the neocloud sector. Investors have become more cautious about the debt required to finance rapid expansion, with CoreWeave (CRWV) at the center of the recent market turmoil.

Neocloud Credit Concerns

CoreWeave lost roughly a quarter of its market value last week during a sharp sell-off in its shares and bonds. Yields on some of its bonds climbed to around 15%, up from about 9.675% when the debt was issued last year.

Both NBIS stock and CRWV shares have fallen nearly 30% this month amid the sell-off. Piper Sandler cut its price target on Nebius by 22% to $185 on Wednesday, warning that neocloud stocks could remain "in the penalty box" until the financing outlook becomes clearer. Gartner has predicted that more than 80% of neocloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030.
